evidence.summary: Round 4 threats: (1) stale-row surfacing through the invoker view - closed by the scope-independent pick (mutation M1 caught); (2) unresolved rows readable by everyone - closed by lineage policies (M2 caught); (3) role spoofing - cip.request_role comes only from the server-side role through the router, forged/non-numeric ids bind nothing, every scoped transaction overwrites it so a pooled backend never carries another request's role (tests); (4) helper misuse - invoker rights, pinned search_path, caller setting restored and asserted, EXECUTE only to roles that read the tables; an error reverts the setting with the (sub)transaction; (5) deploy order - API restarted before the migration; code compatible with 0025 (role unused there); (6) view re-creation dropping the pick - refresh adds it when the helper exists (test).

rationale: Each new trust input or failure path has a control and a test. Residuals: INSERT ... RETURNING / ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE of a row the scoped requester cannot read now fails closed (imports run in workers; shipment write endpoints are admin/steward); background-job scope decision still open; admin compromise exposes all lines.
